classification.difficultyReason: Infer reflection from the partially supplied second petal, extend the symmetry to two further petals, and translate those constructions back into ordered coordinate lists.

spec.description: Shared drawing grid for all four petals. The source requests a grid but supplies no printed figure; students add coordinate axes.
spec.mathematics: A centred coordinate system accommodates coordinates from −4 to 4 in both directions.
spec.answerVisibility: Blank grid only; no petals or completed coordinates.

children.label: a
children.prompt: On a grid, join $(0,0)$ to $(3,1)$ to $(4,2)$ to $(4,4)$ to $(2,4)$ to $(1,3)$ to $(0,0)$ to draw one petal of a flower.

answer.short: The petal in the upper-right quadrant.
answer.worked: Plot the points by moving horizontally first, then vertically. Join $(0,0)$, $(3,1)$, $(4,2)$, $(4,4)$, $(2,4)$, $(1,3)$ and $(0,0)$ in that order.

inlines.text: Complete, and then plot, the following list of points to form a second petal the same shape as the first.

answer.worked: Keep each horizontal coordinate from part a and reverse the sign of each vertical coordinate. Plot and join $(0,0)$, $(3,-1)$, $(4,-2)$, $(4,-4)$, $(2,-4)$, $(1,-3)$ and $(0,0)$ in order.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Draw the remaining two petals of the same shape to complete the flower.

answer.short: Add the two petals in the upper-left and lower-left quadrants.
answer.worked: Copy the two right-hand petals to the left of the vertical axis, keeping each point the same distance from that axis. Join the points in the same order to complete four congruent petals.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Write down the ordered list of points required to draw each of the petals in part c.

answer.worked: For the upper-left petal, reverse the signs of the horizontal coordinates in part a: $(0,0)$, $(-3,1)$, $(-4,2)$, $(-4,4)$, $(-2,4)$, $(-1,3)$, $(0,0)$. For the lower-left petal, reverse the signs of the horizontal coordinates in part b: $(0,0)$, $(-3,-1)$, $(-4,-2)$, $(-4,-4)$, $(-2,-4)$, $(-1,-3)$, $(0,0)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 7; teacher PDF page 35, question 7 graph
spec.description: Complete self-contained answer graph with four congruent closed petals, unit grid and equal coordinate scales.
spec.mathematics: Upper-right path is the supplied path; lower-right reverses y; upper-left reverses x; lower-left reverses both signs.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer editions only; shared by parts a, b and c.
